attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known method proves worst-case residual cap denominator B_N(s,E)>N^{epsilon-sigma-o(1)} for semantic one-sided caps with nonuniform advice.
steps: Assume the generated-OR carrier and the target bridge max{rho,q}<1+epsilon are fixed.
Define B_N(s,E) by adversarial residual positives, not by the first cap or an average distribution.
Apply greedy covering: residual size shrinks by a factor at most 1-1/B_N until at most E positives remain.
OR the K caps and patch the E misses; comparing exponents gives the threshold b+1+sigma<1+epsilon and delta<epsilon.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This only says which cap covers would refute the source lower bound. It does not prove the required cap-scarcity theorem, nor P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Generated-OR residual cap gate for hardness magnification

assumptions: Caps are one-sided: cap(x)=1 implies H_N(x)=1 on the generated range.
The cap circuit may use nonuniform advice about G_N, so the audit is against leakage, not only uniform algorithms.
Equality patches for E missed positive inputs cost O(EN) gates.
Parameters satisfy q in ((1+epsilon)/2,1+epsilon), d>1, rho<1+epsilon.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j<=M} SAT(F_{N,j}(x)), M=N^q, L=(log N)^d, with all F_{N,j} generated by a shared circuit G_N of size N^rho.
target object: SAT on L-bit formulas against SIZE(L^c) for every fixed c; a valid H_N lower bound plus the bridge would imply SAT notin P/poly.
controlled interface: polylog-query generated OR; SAT circuits are substituted only inside generated formulas, while source leakage is audited by one-sided residual caps.
target-preserving condition: d>1 and q,rho<1+epsilon; G_N is shared, the SAT-query length stays polylogarithmic, and no SAT truth-table advice is introduced.
B_N(s,E) is the least B such that every residual positive set R with |R|>E has a one-sided cap of size s hitting at least |R|/B points.

equations.valid_when: Valid when SAT_L has L^c-size nonuniform circuits for fixed c, L=(log N)^d with d>1, and G_N is shared once.

equations.label: residual_greedy_cover
equations.valid_when: Valid when every residual positive set larger than E has a one-sided cap hitting at least a 1/B_N(s,E) fraction.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known method proves K_U^{O(N m^k polylog m)}(TT(SAT_m))>Theta(m^k log m) for explicit SAT. If such a method supplies a poly(N)-constructive large certificate, it becomes a natural-proof object; if it relativizes fully, an oracle-collapse falsifier should apply after oracle-circuit compression is formalized.
steps: Assume a size-s Boolean circuit C decides SAT_m on all m-bit encodings.
Encode m and the gate list of C using O(s log s+log m) bits.
A universal program enumerates all y in {0,1}^m, evaluates C(y), and prints the resulting bit; total time is O(N s polylog s).
Therefore K_U^{O(Ns polylog s)}(x_m)<=O(s log s+log m).
Taking the contrapositive yields the same-slice circuit lower bound at threshold l=Theta(s log s).
If the high-K statement holds i.o. for every s=m^k, then SAT has no polynomial-size nonuniform circuit family, which would be stronger than needed for P != NP.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid quantitative bridge only. It reduces the target to a sharp time-bounded description lower bound and exposes collapse thresholds, but it does not establish that lower bound for SAT.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: time-bounded Kolmogorov transfer gate

assumptions: U is fixed before the lower-bound statement; machine invariance losses are additive constants only.
Circuit descriptions of size s have length at most A s log s under a standard gate-list encoding.
The decompressor has no SAT oracle, no hidden advice, and no nonuniform table except the counted program bits.
The transfer is same-slice: an m-input circuit for SAT_m must generate the length-N truth table x_m.
definitions: source object: x_m=TT(SAT_m), the N=2^m bit truth table of SAT on m-bit encodings, measured by K_U^T(x_m) for a fixed universal deterministic printer U.
target object: nonuniform Boolean circuits SIZE(m^k) deciding SAT on every m-bit encoding, with malformed formulas mapped to 0.
controlled interface: a size-s circuit C is encoded as a counted program that enumerates all y in {0,1}^m and prints C(y) in lexicographic order.
target-preserving condition: the decompressor time bound T(N) is at least the circuit-enumeration time O(N s polylog s) and the program length counts all circuit and advice bits.
K_U^T(x) is the minimum length of a U-program printing exactly x within T(|x|) steps.
The source model is exact-output time-bounded description complexity, not MCSP membership and not a randomized distinguisher.

equations.label: circuit_to_description_upper_bound
equations.latex: SAT_m \in SIZE(s) \Rightarrow K_U^{B N s\log s}(x_m) \le A(s\log s+\log m),\quad N=2^m.
equations.valid_when: Valid when U is fixed, the circuit encoding is explicit, and T covers lexicographic evaluation of all N inputs.

equations.label: contrapositive_size_threshold
equations.latex: K_U^{B N m^k\log m}(x_m)>A m^k\log m \Rightarrow SAT_m \notin SIZE(m^k).
equations.valid_when: Valid when the lower-bound statement uses the same U, the same slice length m, and the same enumeration-time budget.

equations.label: uniform_consequence_if_repeated
equations.latex: [\forall k\ \exists^\infty m:\ K_U^{B_k N m^k\log m}(x_m)>A_k m^k\log m]\Rightarrow SAT\notin P/poly.
equations.valid_when: Valid when the high-K claim holds infinitely often for each circuit exponent and constants absorb uniform simulation overhead.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any O(m^k log m)-bit program running in O(N m^k polylog m) that prints x_m, including one obtained from a small SAT circuit.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Promote as a conditional bridge lemma: it is a valid route-level transfer from a named source model to a named target class, not a proof of the source lower bound or of P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A near-enumeration time-bounded Kolmogorov lower bound for the SAT truth table transfers quantitatively to a same-slice nonuniform circuit lower bound, with threshold Theta(s log s) bits and time Theta(N s polylog s).

assumptions: The formula encoding has at most m variables on m-bit strings.
Malformed encodings are decided by a fixed polynomial-time parser.
For PadSAT_{n,m}, only the first n bits determine the SAT core and the remaining bits are padding.
definitions: x_m=TT(SAT_m) as above.
A trivial SAT printer stores m, loops over all m-bit strings, parses each as a formula, and tries all assignments.
For padded SAT with core length n inside total length m, x_{m,n}=TT(PadSAT_{n,m}).

equations.latex: K_U^{C N 2^m poly(m)}(x_m)\le C\log m = O(\log\log N).

equations.label: padded_bruteforce_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the padded language has core length n and the printer brute-forces only the core assignments.

assumptions: The property is total on all N-bit truth tables.
The same l,T are used for SAT and for excluding every target circuit truth table.

definitions: Usefulness against SIZE(s) follows from KTB-43.1 when l>A s log s and T>=B N s polylog s.
Constructivity by exhaustive program enumeration takes about 2^l T time.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 43 isolates a valid quantitative bridge: K_U^{O(N m^k polylog m)}(TT(SAT_m))>Theta(m^k log m) implies SAT_m notin SIZE(m^k). The same route fails if T is too generous, since brute-force SAT printing gives O(log m) descriptions by time about N^2, and padded cores create sharper collapse thresholds. The barrier status is precise: high-K is large and useful, but not poly(N)-constructive at polynomial circuit thresholds; a constructive proof would naturalize. This is route-level progress, not evidence by itself for P != NP.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Formalize the oracle-circuit version of KTB-43.1 and test whether MCSP-style certificates for K_U^T(x)>l can remain non-natural while preserving the near-linear T=N m^k polylog m threshold.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The audit supplies necessary conditions, not a source theorem: we still need a bounded-D, cap-compatible, non-natural, advice-free invariant with z_m and positive one-certificate complexity at least N^epsilon/m and with actual unrestricted row hardness.
steps: Choose an accepted table T_z of minimum support z_m for the proposed invariant A_m.
Compute T_z by an OR of equality tests to the z_m positive addresses; this gives unrestricted circuit size O(z_m m).
Universal MCSP no-side soundness at threshold N^epsilon therefore implies z_m=Omega(N^epsilon/m).
If A_m has a one-certificate C with p positive literals, the zero completion of C is accepted and has support at most p, so p must satisfy the same lower bound.

If deg_2(A_m)=d and A_m is nonzero, vanishing on all inputs of weight at most d would force every ANF coefficient of degree at most d to vanish by Mobius induction; hence some accepted input has weight at most d.
Combining the previous two bullets gives the syntactic threshold collapse epsilon<=pi+o(1) for degree or positive-certificate exponent pi.
Compose only after this audit with the earlier valid extraction delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This cycle proves a falsifier for invalid carriers and preserves a valid transfer formula; it does not construct a hard truth table, an NP-complete lower bound, or P != NP.

assumptions: N=2^m and T is the full truth table of an m-input Boolean function.
A_m is nonempty and every accepted T is claimed to satisfy Ckt(T)>s_m with s_m=N^epsilon.
Circuits are unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits; equality to one m-bit address has size O(m).
For the ANF clause, A_m is identified with its multilinear polynomial over F_2.
definitions: source object: a family A_m subseteq {0,1}^N with N=2^m, E-uniform decidability/canonicalization, and zero-fill vulnerability z_m=min{|supp(T)|: A_m(T)=1}.
target object: unrestricted Boolean circuit lower bound Ckt(T)>N^epsilon used as an MCSP no-side row, later padded through kappa-density and distinct-image entropy D to an E lower bound.
controlled interface: acceptance A_m(T)=1 may enter the carrier transfer only as a sound assertion that T is a hard truth table in the unrestricted nonuniform circuit model.

target-preserving condition: the predicate is nonempty, advice-free, and universally sound for all accepted tables, or else an E-uniform selector must output a certified hard accepted table without changing kappa, D, or epsilon.
positive one-certificate width pc^+_1(A_m) is the minimum number of coordinates forced to 1 in any genuine one-certificate for A_m.
ANF degree deg_2(A_m) is the degree of the multilinear F_2 polynomial representing the Boolean predicate A_m over truth-table bits.

equations.label: zero_fill_bounds
equations.valid_when: Valid when A_m is nonempty, pc^+_1 counts positive literals in true one-certificates, and the ANF bound uses the F_2 multilinear form.

equations.label: sparse_table_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when T_z has support z_m and unrestricted circuits may hardwire the accepted input addresses using equality tests.

equations.label: soundness_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when A_m is claimed to be universally sound for MCSP no-side threshold N^epsilon against unrestricted nonuniform circuits.

equations.label: syntactic_threshold_collapse

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find one accepted table, term, transcript, or one-certificate with fewer than N^epsilon/O(m) forced one positions; this is a falsifier for universal no-side soundness.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Source-side no-go lemma; it does not prove lower bounds but invalidates broad classes of proposed high-degree or transcript-based MCSP carriers.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a nonempty truth-table invariant used as an MCSP no-side carrier, universal soundness at threshold N^epsilon requires minimum accepted support z_m=Omega(N^epsilon/m). Thus low ANF degree, low positive one-certificate width, DNF accepting terms with few positive literals, or shallow accepting transcripts are quantitative falsifiers for the source.

assumptions: C is a genuine one-certificate: every table extending C is accepted by A_m.
The source consequence requires all accepted tables to be MCSP no-instances at threshold N^epsilon.
The transcript is table-level, not merely a certificate for membership in an opaque generator image.
definitions: transcript source: an accepting computation path or DNF term for a table predicate A_m.
positive transcript width p(C): the number of table coordinates that the transcript forces to value 1.
zero completion T_C^0: the table with ones exactly on the positive coordinates of C and zeros elsewhere.

equations.label: zero_completion_acceptance
equations.valid_when: Valid when the transcript is a true one-certificate and zero filling respects all coordinates fixed to zero by the transcript.

equations.label: transcript_circuit_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the target lower-bound model is unrestricted circuits with hardwired equality tests for the positive coordinates.

equations.label: transcript_exponent_gate

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: An accepting leaf with subthreshold positive width makes the purported source valid only for a weaker epsilon, causing threshold collapse.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantines DNF, decision-tree, local-checking, and low-positive-evidence source proposals.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A verifier-style invariant whose acceptance can be certified by an accepting transcript that fixes p truth-table positions to 1 cannot certify MCSP hardness above O(pm), regardless of how many zero positions or nonlinear checks appear in the transcript.

assumptions: A hard row at threshold N^epsilon is actually supplied or uniformly selected.
Distinct-image unranking is E-uniform and does not leak nonuniform advice.
The source threshold epsilon is at most the verifier access/checkpoint cap alpha_V.
definitions: hard row: an accepted truth table T with unrestricted circuit complexity greater than N^epsilon.
distinct-image entropy D: log_N of the number of distinct accepted tables after E-canonical quotienting.
density padding kappa: the multiplicative exponent loss needed to cover all target input lengths from source lengths.

equations.label: row_extraction_rate
equations.valid_when: Valid when certificate-index or image-rank multiplexing is E-uniform and recovers the hard row without extra advice.

dependency_updates.description: Every table-level MCSP invariant must prove z_m=Omega(N^epsilon/m) and high positive one-certificate complexity before claiming no-side soundness.
Carrier transfer is valid only after sparse accepted tables, contaminated accepted rows, and subthreshold positive transcripts are excluded.
The delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) transfer remains valid, but epsilon must lie below the verifier cap and zero-fill vulnerability cap.
E-uniform canonicalization must expose table-level acceptance or supply an E-uniform hard-row selector; opaque generator membership is insufficient.
The zero-fill obstruction is not a natural-proofs largeness argument; it is a nonuniform sparse-circuit upper bound that invalidates sources even outside the usual largeness barrier.

falsifier: ANF degree N^pi with pi<epsilon on infinitely many source lengths, by the Mobius low-weight accepted input argument.
falsifier: an accepting DNF term, decision-tree leaf, or proof transcript with subthreshold positive width.
falsifier: a verifier whose table-level acceptance is only existential over contaminated easy rows and lacks E-uniform hard-row selection.
falsifier: nonuniform length selection or quotient unranking that hides the hard row in advice.
falsifier: claiming high ANF degree alone while allowing small accepted support or small positive one-certificates.
